label: An OpenBot routine is one sentence in four parts (What, Starts, Does, Until), and goals and check-ins are the same list: a goal is a routine with an outcome, a check-in a routine that only tells.
planRoutine returns exactly three shapes: routine (act on schedule, no outcome), goal (outcome, event start, or run once) with optional schedule, or check-in (tell only with interval).
Event starts are subscriptions: a goal carries source and eventType pairs and runs when asked or when an event wakes it, which is how mail and pull-request starts exist without per-bot trigger lists.
OpenBot bounds standing work: at most one fire per 15 minutes and at most 20 enabled routines per person, because a conversation accumulates work without noticing.
The fatigue rule is about worth, not retries: one message on the first failure after a success, ten consecutive failures switch the routine off, and re-enabling restarts the count.
Missed windows are skipped, not replayed: the next run is a stamp, and an offline month advances the stamp occurrence by occurrence without firing the backlog.

Skilled bots' cron path is exact by construction: every cron string becomes launchd calendar dictionaries that fire exactly as cron or is refused with a named invariant, and the translator is the only cron reader.
Skilled bots' triggers are cron, queue, git-hook and manual, with git-hook opt-in per repository, and only cron triggers can be installed as schedules.
The queue drain routes strictly: claim by rename, quarantine refusals and paused or held requests, retry failures to three, and stop the pass on a setup fault with the request returned.

Mapping the four parts: What is the BOT.md body, Starts at a time is cron, Starts on an event is a queue trigger fed by a producer, Does only tell is local-only delivery, Until you stop it is the disabled switch; Until an outcome needs one optional until block plus a completion check, and the routine list is a read over BOT.md files and the status index.
